page: Amazon Web Services c8g.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 model running at 2.8 GHz. The processor lacks hyperthreading, providing exactly one thread per core. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The server achieves top-tier status in uncached memory bandwidth, with read speeds of 395.06 GB/sec and write speeds of 184.52 GB/sec. Multi-core execution is highly efficient, as evidenced by top-tier scores in Geekbench multi-core testing and software compilation using Clang. Database operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the top decile, while single-core performance and cryptographic operations align with average baseline expectations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Graviton-based architecture delivers high compute density and memory throughput per resource unit without the overhead of hyperthreading. This makes the c8g.12xlarge highly suitable for compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-sensitive workloads. Recommended applications include software compilation, high-throughput web serving, database operations, multi-threaded decompression, and medium-scale language model inference.
